@graph.name: Entry 49: the affine deficit $\delta_5 = \varepsilon_{\mathrm{coast}} k_1 + k_2$ — global vs per rider
@graph.text: No on both counts. k1 > 0 is solid (0.92, 95% CI [0.46, 2.73] excludes zero, so the limit does over-credit), but the two-parameter fit is UNIDENTIFIED: the derived slope 1−k1 has CI [−1.73, +0.54], spanning inverted to substantially positive, because k1 and k2 trade off. The form is also dominated by the flat constant it nests at k1 = 1 — that has the lower BIC with half the parameters and identical held-out error — so the second parameter buys nothing. The per-rider arm (14 parameters) wins in sample and on within-rider held-out, but its fits disagree on SIGN across riders, one stays pinned to a bound, and it is the only form that pushes ε outside [0,1]. Frozen ε₀ = 0.13, keeping the geometry at full weight, has the best held-out error and bias of every form with fewer than 14 parameters.
